Build archetypes and energy: a visual guide

Concept companion to build-archetypes.md and energy-system.md (2026-10-31). Nothing here is built; names are placeholders.

How to read this guide

A visual companion to docs/design/build-archetypes.md and docs/design/energy-system.md. Those two docs are the source of truth. Nothing here is built. Part renders come from the game's own renderer; ship layouts and new-part sketches are rough concepts.

Power types

Steady along wires
Surge by touch only, from a bank into what it touches
Thermal along wires
Exotic along wires

Hues follow the energy doc (cyan, white-violet, orange, green-gold), tuned so cyan and violet stay apart for colour-blind readers. Each type also carries a letter (S, U, T, X). Exact hexes: proposed.

Fit of a part to an archetype

C●core, and named in the docs ("Relies on" list or an energy-doc layout)
Ccore, this guide's proposal
ggood: fits the plan
ppoor: works, off-plan
no: works against it

Activities

Sstrong: a first pick
ookay
wweak

From build-archetypes.md §4, unchanged.

Layouts

Two views of each ship: parts (each cell's part, by token; dashed white outline = new part) and power view (a hangar-overlay mock: circuits coloured by type and lettered, wires with flow dots, hatched violet = capacitor bank, ⚡ = fed by touch, split cell = dual-fed, red dashes = warning). Token legends sit under each layout. Wires are drawn as the shortest tree from a generator: the docs only fix which circuit a part is on, not the wire route.

1. The archetypes at a glance

Fifteen builds, each the best answer to something and a poor answer to most things. Each card: the concept layout (power view), the closest existing ship, strong and weak activities, energy shape and the existing parts it is built on.

3. Archetype by archetype

For each: the concept layout (parts and power view), the closest existing ship, how it plays in each activity, the existing parts it rests on, the new parts it needs, its energy shape, and its counters. Layouts not from the energy doc are marked proposed layout.

Da Dancer: dodge duelist

Light, twitchy, never where the bullet is.
BossEscortMiningHaulingTravelColdSiege / nestParty supportPvP zone
SwwwowooS

Sparrow T is light and small but has no strafers or turrets; nothing existing is built to dodge.

Loop
Read the telegraph, tap a burst strafe sideways through the gap, snap back to shoot during the boss's recovery window.
Counters
Sustained area denial (Cloudmaker/mortar fields, pools), homing that tracks a strafe, getting caught empty after a chain of dodges.
Party role
Boss 'point' pilot: pulls the boss's aim and dives into windows. Pairs with a Warden behind it.

Energy shape

Spiky. Big drive store, small gun draw. Starves its guns if it dodges too much.

Illustrative shape of stored charge in a 30 s fight, not simulated from game numbers. Energy-doc identity: Surge kicks on strafers; guns on a circuit the dodge can't drain (energy §5.1).

Maw Lurker (enemy) carries a railgun and missiles on a narrow frame: the closest existing shape.

Loop
Hold range, line up the nose, fire slow heavy shots, back off when something closes. Repositions often, fires rarely.

Party role
Removes key parts (shield emitters, weapon pods) and paints targets for others.

Loop
Charge a short-range jump; blink into the opening; dump capacitors into the target; blink or burst out before the window closes.
Counters
Being caught in the cooldown; enemies that punish proximity (Scrap Mother claws); EMP during the charge.
Party role
Finisher: waits for the Disruptor's stun or the boss's vent, then bursts.

Extreme burst. Two banks, both full before a strike, both empty after.

4. Energy system visuals

Local circuits: today vs proposal A

Brownout: what a circuit can deliver

Rule A3: steady loads take their share first, then burst consumers in priority order (engines first by default). A brownout is a visible state: the circuit flashes, guns reload slower, engines push less, lasers dim.

Discharge rates per store type

Charge left in one full cell when drained flat out (proposal A2 placeholder numbers). Capacity says how long, discharge says how hard.

Battery (7 s)Heavy Bank (20 s)Drive Cell (5 s)Capacitor (0.8 s)Core battery (20 s) (dashed)Heavy Bank and the core battery both take 20 s: their lines overlap.
discharge per cell per second
capacity per cell

Capacitors only discharge into parts they touch (A4); the core battery feeds any circuit at a trickle (A5); Drive Cells serve engines only.

Power types and the reaction table

typemade bytravelscost / catchgood at
SteadyCell Reactor, Isotope Pile, Fusion Plant, Overclock Reactor; stored in Battery / Heavy Bankalong wiresnone: the baselineefficiency, endurance, everything works
SurgeCapacitor banks (charged from any circuit); new Pulse Dynamoby touch only, from a bank into what it touchessmall capacity, long refill; banks are fragilespikes: charged shots, kicks, instant shield restores
Thermalnew Plasma Burner (maybe Overclock Reactor: open question)along wiresburns propellant while used; adds heatraw power, afterburn, burning effects, warmth in the cold
Exotic (later)Resonance Core (boss-artefact recipe, one per ship)along wiresrare; one per shipwaking up the boss legendaries' extra behaviour
consumer Steady Surge (touching a bank) Thermal
Projectile guns
cannon, autocannon, railgun, flak…		as nowCharged shot: a shot after a pause takes a bank packet and hits harder and faster. Fire rate unchanged.Hot rounds: a short burn on hull hit; the gun adds heat
Beams and lasers
Glint, Cutter, Lance…		as nowPulse: bigger, shorter pulses (the bank sets the peak)Longer reach, more heat
Engines
as nowKick: boost becomes a short fixed impulse per bank packetAfterburn: higher rated speed and boost; burns propellant, adds heat
Shields
normal regenFlash restore: when it breaks, the bank re-raises part of it at oncenot accepted
Utility
jump coil, scanner, miner		as nowjump coil: shorter charge; scanner: pingbore and miner: melt (faster, hotter); Heater Core → warmth

Energy doc B3: one table by category, not by model (about 12 cells to learn). Existing models keep accepting Steady (B4: types add, never remove). Ammo weapons keep using ammo; the type changes what their energy buys.

A part touching two circuits of different types runs a combo (energy B5). The hangar shows it as a two-colour ring and the combo name.

7. Progression: what opens when

Every existing model at its unlock level, by lane. Side = a new verb against earlier models of its family; up = the same verb with bigger numbers (this guide's reading). New parts sit in their proposed unlock bands. Archetype bars run from the level its first two core parts are unlocked to the level its doc-named kit is complete.

side: new verbup: same verb, bigger numbersbase: first of familyproposed new-part band◆ first new part for that archetype

Of the 65 models: 28 family bases, 19 sidegrades, 18 upgrades. The upgrades are where archetypes §3.5 suggests flattening damage and keeping armour penetration as the only vertical stat.

8. Findings

  1. Four archetypes have almost nothing existing to start from: Carrier (1 core model, 1 named in the docs), Warden (4 core models, 3 named in the docs), Salvage Tug (1 core model, 1 named in the docs), Ghost (2 core models, 2 named in the docs). The thinnest kits overall: Ca 1, Tu 1, Gh 2, Bl 3, Fr 4, Wa 4. The Carrier's only anchor is Rustjaw's Hive, a legendary gated by a boss part. Warden has no part that helps another ship (Constructor is the nearest), Salvage Tug has no tow, Ghost has no signature system (enemies' aggro range exists, nothing scales it). These need their first new part before they exist at all.
  2. 15 existing models are core to no archetype: Pip, Twinlink, Strobe, Overpulse, Dart, Swarm, Coilgun, Lance, Cinder Bloom, Prism Splitter, Phase Cannon, Plasma Drive, Cell Reactor, Battery, Flicker Screen. Most are fine as "good" generalists; the Pulse family (Strobe, Overpulse) and Coilgun are the clearest candidates to be given a job (Overpulse as the Arc Bank rework, Coilgun as a Surge-fed rail).
  3. Conductive Steel fits nothing. Its conductive trait only matters for the legacy conduit hazard term (energy §1.2 #8). A use: plate that lets touching capacitors count as one bank across a gap, or that carries Surge one cell.
  4. The Capacitor carries five archetypes (Da, Bl, Bw, In, Al). The touch rule (A4) decides how all five play, so its numbers and the bank-merging rule are the most load-bearing tuning in both docs.
  5. Freighter, Pathfinder and Ghost share one kit (Drift Sail + Isotope Pile). Without cargo mass, heat/warmth and a signature system they converge on the same ship; each needs its own mechanic first (archetypes §5 #3, #9, #11).
  6. Several doc kits finish after level 30: Bombard (L38), Disruptor (L35), Alpha Striker (L38). Leviathan (L38), Blackout (L35) and Hammerhead (L33) are core to them. Either these archetypes are late-game by design, or their kits need an earlier sidegrade.
  7. Exotic power has no archetype. It upgrades legendaries only; no archetype is built around it, which matches the doc's "later, if at all".
  8. Burst Strafer vs Surge "Kick", and Discharge Capacitor vs Capacitor-as-bank, overlap: the energy doc turns every capacitor into a fast-dumping Surge bank and makes any engine touching one kick, which covers most of what those two new parts do.
  9. Interceptor and Blinker share one energy-doc layout (§5.6). This guide gives the Blinker its own (separate gun and drive circuits plus a Blink Coil); the Ignition Kick stays with both.
  10. Only 2 library ships are direct starting points (Bulwark, Prospector); Corsair and Ceres Hauler are close. Most archetypes' nearest silhouette is an enemy design.

9. Open questions (decisions the visuals had to guess)

  1. Power-type colours: exact hexes (Steady #18b4d0, Surge #b57cff, Thermal #f06a1a, Exotic #b3c02a) are proposed; the doc's "white-violet" is pushed to a stronger violet so it doesn't collide with cyan for deuteranopes.
  2. Unlock bands for every new part are proposed (8–15, 16–23, 24–31, 30+). Should new verbs land in each 8-level band, per archetypes §3.5?
  3. Is the Burst Strafer still a part if Surge on engines already gives a Kick? Same for the Discharge Capacitor once all capacitors are banks. (Proposed here: keep them as the Surge-only versions with charges and the fastest dump.)
  4. Blink Coil's power: drive-store bite (archetypes) or a Surge bank (like the Snap Coil)? Shown here as Steady + Surge.
  5. Radiator: a heat part, not a power type. Shown with the Thermal pip because it only matters on hot circuits; it could carry no pip.
  6. Does a Pulse Dynamo count as part of the bank it touches (so a bank can bridge through it)? The layouts assume yes.
  7. Wire routing in the power views is a shortest tree from a generator; the docs only fix which circuit a cell is on. For the Freighter, the doc's loop is drawn as spine + outer ring.
  8. Fit ratings other than C● are this guide's reading, especially for materials (which the docs only discuss as a triangle). Worth a pass by Kieran.
  9. Upgrade vs sidegrade labels on existing models are a reading of their stats and descriptions, not a doc decision.
  10. Nine archetype layouts are new (Longshot, Blinker, Carrier, Pathfinder, Prospector, Warden, Disruptor, Salvage Tug, Ghost). In particular: Warden with two equal circuits and a divert; Prospector with a dual-fed Melt Bore braced by an Anchor; Pathfinder using a capacitor bank for a Snap Coil.
  11. Shield Projector and Repair Beam: Steady here. Should they take Surge (a burst heal / flash shield on an ally)?
  12. Hangar warnings in the mockups ("Shooting the bank row cuts surge from…", load-test result lines, HUD bank pips) extend energy §6 wording; the exact UI is open.

About this guide

Generated by docs/design/guide/build/build.mjs from build/data.mjs (archetypes, fits, new parts, layouts) and the game's data/ships/models.json, materials.json, pieces.json. Part renders: npm run render -- --batch @list --dir docs/design/guide/img/parts with model:<id> --stub 0 --zoom 2 --w 260 --h 260 --bg transparent --light hangar (and material:<id>), cropped to content; ship renders: ship:<id> / boss:<id> at 420×420.
